claims.claim: Activation/trustline reserves apply only to unsponsored G-accounts in this comparison.

sources.quote: Stellar account balances for issued assets are always stored in trust lines, and Stellar contract balances for issued assets are always stored in a contract data entry.
Anything that increases the minimum balance can be sponsored (account creation, offers, trustlines, data entries, signers, claimable balances).

claims.notes: Contract-data balances still have resource and rent costs.

claims.claim: Fee bumps or relayers pay transaction fees.

sources.quote: Use fee-bump transactions to pay for transaction fees on behalf of another account without re-signing the transaction.
Both the Begin Sponsoring Future Reserves and the End Sponsoring Future Reserves operations must appear in the sponsorship transaction.

claims.notes: The page assigns the sponsored reserve requirements to the sponsoring account.

claims.claim: USDC uses its Stellar Asset Contract interface and balance.

sources.quote: The Stellar Asset Contract (SAC) is the built-in contract interface to assets on the Stellar network.

claims.notes: The page states that contract-address balances use contract-data entries.

claims.claim: Token-relay or hosted-facilitator designs use caps, liquidity, and abuse controls.

sources.quote: Monitor Relayer Balance; Configure Swap Schedule; Set Appropriate Limits: Configure max_allowed_fee to prevent excessive fees.

claims.notes: The provider guide also uses allowed_tokens and token-address validation.

evidenceLines: Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/stellar-asset-contract — G-address issued balances use trustlines; C-address balances use contract data.
